investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 121 s (remote-agent-create), 143 s (remote-agent-state), and 146 s (remote-agent-runtime), the eval runner timed out before any VM was assigned, leaving all required evidence fields empty. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this diagnosis is scoped to the AURA observability eval.

No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 121 s (remote-agent-create), 143 s (remote-agent-state), and 146 s (remote-agent-runtime), the eval runner timed out before any VM was assigned, leaving all required evidence fields empty. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this diagnosis is scoped to the AURA observability eval.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-18 because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained stuck until the eval timed out and no evidence was ever collected.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible for peer-pod VM workloads and both are at capacity; the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never completed, the remote agent was never provisioned, and the eval produced zero evidence — leaving all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) missing and the message assertion ("hello from aura") unverifiable. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

If the selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, capacity that previously existed may now be unreachable.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes is too small to absorb concurrent eval probe runs, causing contention when multiple checks run in close succession (remote-agent-create at 12:38, remote-agent-state at 12:40, remote-agent-runtime at 12:43).
